practices.practice: Use a single MongoClient (one shared client instance per process) and configure connection-pool sizing and timeouts rather than creating a client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single MongoClient/MongoClient-equivalent instance (singleton) shared across the process and threads; do not create a new client per request. Configure sensible pool sizes (maxPoolSize) and timeouts at client creation.

practices.practice: Set driver timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, maxIdleTimeMS) and require TLS in the connection string so clients fail fast on network problems and use secure transport.

practices.practice: Handle transient faults by implementing retries with exponential backoff and making write operations idempotent (do not rely solely on driver retries); design retry limits and respect Retry-After when returned.

practices.practice: Harden network access: restrict public access with firewall rules, prefer Private Link (private endpoints) for production, and use Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC plus customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest when required.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and collect data-plane logs into Log Analytics (or other sinks) to monitor request charge (RU), latency, 429s, partition RU consumption and index usage; use $explain to measure per-query RU.

practices.practice: Create the indexes your queries need (single-field and compound) and prefer creating or modifying indexes after bulk data loads to avoid write overhead; track createIndex progress and be aware unique index builds may block operations.
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Index fields used in frequent equality filters and sorts and use compound indexes when queries filter or sort by multiple fields together.
practices.prior_belief: Index all fields used in frequent equality and sort/filter patterns (e.g., sku, timestamp, competitor_id, active flag). Use compound indexes for queries that filter by multiple fields together (e.g., {'sku':1,'timestamp':-1}).
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB indexing compound indexes best practices

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) on a timestamp field (commonly the _ts system timestamp or a custom TTL field) to automatically expire time-series/metric documents and reduce storage and RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) for time-series / metric collections (demand metrics) to automatically purge old documents and reduce storage and RU consumption.
practices.source_name: Expire data with Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB and per-document TTL
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TTL index expireAfterSeconds _ts

practices.practice: Use projections (select only required fields) on find/aggregate queries to reduce network payload and RU consumption when you don't need full documents.
practices.prior_belief: When reading documents for decision-making, use projections to fetch only required fields (e.g., price, sku, timestamp, margin rules) to reduce network and request charge.
practices.source_name: find

practices.practice: Avoid large skip-based (offset) pagination for high offsets; prefer server-provided continuation tokens or range-/cursor-based paging (e.g., timestamp or id cursors) for efficiency and determinism.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid large skip-based pagination for high offsets; prefer range-based pagination (e.g., timestamp or _id cursors) to keep queries efficient and low-cost.

practices.practice: Use single-document atomic operations (findOneAndUpdate / findAndModify / $set / $inc) for per-item updates; for multi-document atomic work, use multi-document transactions only where supported and tested.
practices.prior_belief: Perform single-document atomic updates with find_one_and_update (with a filter) or update operators ($set, $inc). Use the operation's returned document (or returnDocument option) to confirm the write.

practices.practice: Implement optimistic concurrency control using system _etag (ETag) or a version field and conditional updates (If-Match / if-match) to detect and avoid lost updates.
practices.prior_belief: Use optimistic concurrency control for price updates to avoid lost updates: include a version field or use a server-side optimistic check (filter by previous value or _etag) in the find-and-update filter.

practices.practice: Model documents for your query patterns: denormalize product and pricing data where reads benefit, and store frequently-changing telemetry/metrics in separate collections to avoid large document churn.
practices.prior_belief: Design collection documents for query patterns: keep product and pricing data denormalized enough to read pricing decisions in a single document where practical, and store frequently-changed telemetry/metrics in separate collections to avoid document churn.

practices.practice: When SRV/discovery returns multiple nodes (query-from-any-node / sharded clusters), size maxPoolSize per node because drivers maintain one pool per discovered server; adjust total pool budget accordingly.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB query from any node maxPoolSize per node guidance

practices.practice: For vector search, store numeric vectors in a dedicated field (number[]) and create a vector index (kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw, or vector-diskann), then tune algorithm parameters (e.g., HNSW m/efConstruction, IVF numLists, DiskANN lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree) to trade recall vs latency.

practices.practice: You can create and drop vector indexes after container creation (no need to define vector indexing at container creation time), but pick an algorithm appropriate to dataset size (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN guidance).

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document ACID transactions, but they have practical limits (transaction lifetime/timeout) and behavior differs by server version and tooling—test transactions and their limits on your target cluster before using them in production.

practices.practice: Creating a unique index on an existing collection can block reads and writes for the duration of the build; plan unique-index creation carefully (create on empty collections or schedule maintenance), and track build progress.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB unique index build blocks collection guidance

practices.practice: Use explain() / $explain and RU charge metrics to validate that a query uses an index and to measure its RU cost before rolling it into production.

practices.practice: Make seed and provisioning scripts idempotent: use upserts or conditional inserts and avoid destructive operations so seeding can be safely repeated.
practices.prior_belief: Make seed scripts idempotent: check for existing documents, use upserts or conditional inserts, and avoid destructive operations so seeding can be safely repeated against the same database.

practices.practice: Choose a partition/shard key with high cardinality that aligns with your dominant query or write patterns to avoid hot partitions and uneven shard utilization; plan sharding only when a collection exceeds a single-shard capacity.
practices.prior_belief: Provision collections (containers) with an appropriate partition/shard key chosen for even distribution at scale; avoid high-cardinality hotspots on a single partition key value (e.g., avoid using a constant or low-cardinality field as the partition key).

practices.practice: When using CMK for encryption at rest, ensure Azure DocumentDB's managed identity has Key Vault access and that Key Vault networking and policies allow the cluster to reach the key, because misconfiguration can render the cluster inaccessible.

practices.practice: Tune client connection options such as serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socket/connect timeouts, and maxPoolSize to your network and workload so operations fail fast when the DB is unreachable and to control total open connections.
practices.prior_belief: Tune client connection options: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS, and heartbeatFrequency appropriately for your network and app needs so that operations fail fast when the DB is unreachable.

practices.practice: When using MongoDB driver-level consistency primitives, remember Azure DocumentDB maps driver readConcern/readPreference and writeConcern to the service consistency model; writeConcern may be ignored—use Cosmos/DocumentDB consistency controls and test behavior in your target server version.
practices.prior_belief: Use appropriate readConcern/readPreference and writeConcern settings consistent with your consistency needs: prefer stronger guarantees for financial/price writes and lower-latency weaker guarantees for non-critical reads if necessary.

practices.practice: When seeding or migrating, create indexes after bulk data load where possible and use nonblocking createIndex for large historical datasets (issue createIndex asynchronously and track progress with db.currentOp()).

notes:
I performed open discovery across connection, authentication, indexing, TTL, vector search, transactions, sharding/partitioning, retries, monitoring, and security using Microsoft Learn / Azure docs. Where a prior belief matched the public documentation I reused the discovered practice (marked prior_knowledge_confirmed). One prior belief (K19 about writeConcern/readConcern) was contradicted by Azure docs: driver writeConcern is mapped/ignored and you should use service consistency controls; and one prior belief (K20 about not sending secrets to models) had no explicit Azure DocumentDB documentation addressing models/LLMs, so it remains prior_knowledge_only; searches tried for that are listed above.
